articles.title: DeepSeek Just Made Its 75% Price Cut Permanent. Indian IT's Margin Problem Got Worse.
articles.excerpt: The Chinese AI lab's V4-Pro model now costs 7 to 17 times less than comparable Western models. For Infosys, TCS, and Wipro, the implications are existential. For Indian startups, it's a gift.
articles.nri_angle: India's $250 billion IT services industry — employer of millions of Indian-origin workers globally — faces direct margin pressure from plummeting AI inference costs. Meanwhile, Indian AI startups like O-Health and Sarvam AI can now access frontier-class models at a fraction of Western pricing, potentially leapfrogging their Silicon Valley peers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Coding Assistants Are Rewriting the H-1B Job Market. The Engineers They Replace Won't Get a 60-Day Grace Period.
articles.excerpt: Companies are hiring fewer developers, paying more for AI talent, and increasingly preferring green card holders. For hundreds of thousands of Indian H-1B workers, the shift is existential.
articles.nri_angle: An estimated 300,000-plus Indian nationals hold H-1B visas in the United States, a disproportionate number of them software developers at FAANG companies, Indian IT services firms, and mid-size tech employers. The shift from hiring coders to hiring AI-augmented systems thinkers directly threatens the traditional career path that brought most of them to America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel Just Made Its First Manufacturing Move in India. The $3.3 Billion Bet Is on Packaging, Not Chips.
articles.excerpt: A new substrate facility in Odisha positions India inside the advanced packaging supply chain that powers every AI server and smartphone on the planet.
articles.nri_angle: Indian semiconductor professionals in the US — many of whom work at Intel, TSMC, and Applied Materials — now have a credible career path in India's chip ecosystem. For NRI investors, the broader India Semiconductor Mission portfolio (Tata Dholera, Micron Gujarat, CG Semi Sanand, and now Intel Odisha) is becoming a real asset class.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bajaj Finserv Is Spending ₹2,000 Crore to Build India's AI Startup Factory. IIT Bombay Is the Lab.
articles.excerpt: The financial conglomerate's new Finserv Intelligence programme blends venture capital, academic research, and enterprise access — a model India's deep-tech ecosystem has been missing.
articles.nri_angle: NRI founders building in AI, cybersecurity, or quantum computing now have a serious Indian corporate backer that offers more than capital — Bajaj Finserv's ecosystem includes Bajaj Finance, India's largest NBFC, plus insurance, asset management, and consumer lending arms. For diaspora technologists considering a return-to-India startup, this is the kind of institutional backing that previously only existed in the Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
